title: Ten Thousand Updates, One Paint: update() and repaint(), and Drawing Only What Changed

questions.question: A sensor adds 10000 samples and calls update() for each, before the event loop runs. How many paints?
questions.explanation: 0 paints inside the calls and 1 after.

questions.question: What does repaint() do that update() does not?
options: Paints at once, every time it is called

questions.question: What does update(rect) tell Qt?
options: Which part of the widget is out of date, and the paint event carries it
questions.explanation: The rectangle was 1 pixel wide and 100 high.

questions.question: A paintEvent draws all 300 columns although the event is for one. What is wrong?
options: The work is done and thrown away: the loop should go over only the columns in the event rectangle
questions.explanation: One sample went over 1 column, where a full update went over 300.

questions.question: Columns 10 and 200 are updated before the loop runs. How many paints, over how many columns?
options: 1, over 191: the event is the bounding rectangle
questions.explanation: The rectangle ran from x = 10 to x = 200.

questions.question: Which thread may paint a widget?
options: The main thread of the process only, never a widget thread
questions.explanation: Lesson 09-13 is about getting the data there.
